title: Chess, But SCP-2774 Is Inside Your Head
summary: Standard chess vs Stockfish with a neutral SCP-2774 'sloth' piece starting on b4. The sloth seizes the free will of every piece adjacent to it: after each Black move, the sloth moves one square and then scans the squares around it starting at the top-left and going clockwise; each adjacent piece (either colour) found is forced to make a random legal move, which can chain onto newly-adjacent pieces. Narrator plays aggressively to feed pieces to the sloth and wins in one game when the sloth moves a blocking pawn, letting his queen capture the black king.
rules: Standard chess otherwise; White = player, Black = Stockfish.
Neutral SCP-2774 (sloth) starts on b4; it cannot be captured (pieces cannot move onto it) [inferred from 'this pawn can't move onto the sloth'].
Turn order: White move, Black move, then the sloth acts.

Sloth action: it moves one square (roams, sometimes toward pieces), then checks each of its 8 neighbouring squares in clockwise order starting with the top-left square (from White's view: a5,b5,c5,c4,c3,b3,a3,a4 when on b4).

Every piece found on a neighbour square is forced to make one random legal(pseudo-legal) move, possibly a capture; a piece that moves into a not-yet-checked neighbour square can be triggered again ('checked D4 and found another pawn... let's make it take this knight').
Random moves ignore check: kings can be left capturable; capturing the king wins (king capture used to end the game).
If a piece has no moves (e.g. pawn blocked by the sloth), nothing happens for it.
win_condition: Capture/checkmate the Stockfish king (game ended by queen capturing the exposed king after a sloth-forced move).
